cost: a duplicate finding id and a stale digest were committed and pushed, then repaired in a follow-up commit
what: Two sessions appended to logs/improvement-log.jsonl within seven minutes. expected: an append-only log tolerates two writers; that is most of the point of append-only

what: `preflight-build-config` reported `[dead-target]` on the `lint` step, which is correct as declared and not a defect: lint tees the solution checker's stdout into $ARTIFACT_DIR/solution-checker/ and then asserts the file is non-empty with `test -s`, in the SAME command. cost: three failed shapes for one sub-area attribute across two days; the reviewer had reasonably concluded it was a platform limitation
what: A site-map SubArea's Url attribute is a URL, not a set of parameters to append. Three shapes were tried and failed: (1) Entity= alongside Url="?pagetype=..." — opened the table's default view; (2) Url="&pagetype=...&viewType=1039" with no Entity, which the SITE MAP designer itself wrote — the sub-pages vanished from play mode entirely and the APP designer rejected the value saying it expects a web resource. That error was the answer. GROUND TRUTH came from a Microsoft-authored MANAGED sitemap in the same environment: the 'Power Platform Environment Settings' app carries 25 sub-areas with Url values, every one of them a ROOT-RELATIVE path — Url="/main.aspx?pagetype=control&controlName=..." and Url="/tools/externappmanagement/externappmanagement.aspx".

root_cause: The Url attribute was inferred from the shape of a querystring rather than read off a real instance. The site map designer compounded it by persisting a fragment the app designer then rejects, so the platform disagreed with itself and both halves were trusted in turn.
why_it_was_never_caught: nothing validates a SubArea Url. `verify-shipped-content.py` reads etn= out of it to prove the table is reachable, which passes on any string containing etn=<name> — including two shapes that render nothing at all.
lesson: A site-map SubArea Url must be a ROOT-RELATIVE URL — a leading slash, then ?, then the query string: Url="/main.aspx?pagetype=entitylist&etn=<table>&viewid=<guid>". A bare `&pagetype=...` fragment is not a URL; the app designer rejects it with 'expects a web resource' and the sub-area disappears from play mode. Read the shape off a Microsoft-authored managed sitemap in the same org — 'Power Platform Environment Settings' has 25 examples — rather than inferring it. AND NOTE: a leading-slash URL carries no host, so it is environment-independent and does NOT breach C-TECH-047; the solution-awareness objection to hardcoding a URL is answered by the relative form, not by avoiding URLs.
